ship.header: Captain's log, stardate 80240.7. Zada, Hedron Grinder.
ship.situation: We put in at Alex's house on Moraga Way in Orinda, three vessels in the sector: Alex, Stuart and ourselves. This was the first of four engagements of the evening, and the ship was to fly only this one. She went out as printed, with nothing altered since she was commissioned.
ship.narrative: I set one opening hand aside and then chose to keep the next: a clean run of land, a set of light one-cost orders, and the copying half of the ship's method, Storm-Kiln Artist among it. What it did not hold was a single member of the crew. Zada's whole method is to take one order and repeat it for every hand aboard; with no hands aboard there is nothing to repeat, and so nothing came of the hour that followed. I want it stated plainly rather than buried in the manner of it: the test for a hand I choose to keep is the presence of crew, not the number of cheap orders I can give. I applied the wrong test, because the cards themselves were good ones and I read them instead of the requirement.

assessment.text: The engagement was decided before a card was turned, and the decision was mine. I hold a test for an opening hand and I did not apply it; the hand read well, I let that stand in for whether it could do anything, and I should have set it aside as I had set aside the one before.

I find no fault with the ship. She is as she was printed, her fittings did what they are built to do the moment there was anything for them to act upon, and there was not; that is a matter of what I brought aboard and not of how she is put together.
Some share of it belongs to the draw, which offered nothing afterwards that would have corrected the keep. I record that and I do not lean on it.

orders.text: I have ordered Engineering to leave the ship exactly as she stands. Nothing in this engagement is chargeable to her fittings, and she remains as printed.

I have ordered Helm to enter the condition in the standing instructions, where it will be read before an opening hand is judged: the route requires crew aboard early, and copying machinery on its own does not open it.

ship.coda: A ship built to repeat one order to every hand aboard is a quiet vessel with nobody aboard to hear it. I have now had that demonstrated at some length.

ship.header: Captain's log, stardate 80244.7. Zada, Hedron Grinder.
ship.situation: We made Oliver's, five vessels in the sector: Oliver, Tom, Alex, Ryan and ourselves. This was the first of three engagements of the evening. Three mono-red vessels sat in that sector, Oliver and Tom among them, with further red besides.
ship.narrative: I chose to keep an opener of three basic lands, a utility land that comes in ready only when three basics are already down and brings a small body with it when it does, and Krenko, Mob Boss. I liked it at the time. It carried land and it carried a piece of machinery, and it carried no small crew, which is the fuel this ship burns; the light orders sat elsewhere in the ship, the ones in my hand were the expensive kind, and that half never turned over. The method was never assembled. Oliver finished every seat in the sector on the fifth turn, making bodies off his own Krenko and turning them into damage. Plainly, then, and for the second time: crew presence is what gates a hand I choose to keep, and I kept one that had none.

assessment.text: The same error as four nights before, made after I had already written the rule down. I kept the hand for its land and for a piece of machinery I am fond of, and I did not ask the one question that settles it; that is an error of judgment on my part, and its being the second of its kind is the part worth recording.

The ship did no worse than the hand permitted. Her light orders are what turn her over, and the ones I was holding cost too much to be given early, so nothing accumulated. Whether that is a matter of how the list is weighted or simply of what I drew, I am not persuaded either way.

The sector was against us on its own terms. Three vessels running red, one of them finishing on the fifth turn, leaves a ship that needs several turns to assemble anything without the turns to do it in.

orders.text: I have ordered Helm to hold the standing condition without exception and to state it where it is read first: no opening hand is kept on the strength of its machinery alone.
I have ordered Ops to report on the cost of the ship's light orders, and on how many of them can be given inside the first three turns against how many I am likely to be holding that cannot.
I have ordered Tactical to report on what we carry against a sector that finishes on the fifth turn.

ship.coda: Twice now, four days apart, and both times from a hand I chose to keep for the way it read. This one is in the log.
